title: Measuring the Amount a Coverage Answers For on Bench Labour
content:
# Costing Note: Measuring the Amount a Coverage Answers For on Bench Labour

This note defines the amount a protection coverage answers for on a work order of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service, and works that amount to a figure.

## The quantities

**The measured bench labour.** The bench labour standing priced on the work order, measured as booked.

**The share the coverage carries.** The whole of the measured bench labour, 100 percent of it.

**The step taken off that share.** Nothing: 0 percent is taken off the share.

**The line the credit is measured against.** The most recent bench labour line standing on the work order.

**The benefit still available.** The benefit still available on the coverage held on the piece, as the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans records show it.

## The amount answered for

What the coverage answers for is the measured bench labour taken at the share the coverage carries less any step taken off that share, and it is never more than the amount standing on the priced line the credit is measured against, nor more than the benefit still available on the coverage; the figure is rounded to the nearest cent. The amount that stands is therefore the lowest of those three: the measured bench labour taken at the share net of the step, the amount on the line the credit is measured against, and the benefit still available.

The deductible under the coverage is collected at the counter and is never taken off here.

## Worked to a figure on hypothetical inputs

Take a hypothetical work order carrying three bench labour lines, priced at 180.00 USD, 250.00 USD and 210.00 USD, the last of them the most recently posted; and a coverage on the piece with 900.00 USD of benefit still available.

- The measured bench labour is the bench labour standing priced on the order as booked, 640.00 USD.
- Taken at the share of 100 percent and with 0 percent taken off that share, the labour answered for is 640.00 USD.
- The line the credit is measured against is the most recent bench labour line, 210.00 USD.
- The credit is the lowest of 640.00 USD, 210.00 USD and 900.00 USD, rounded to the nearest cent: 210.00 USD.

Had the same order shown only 150.00 USD of benefit still available, the credit would have been 150.00 USD instead, that being then the lowest of the three.
